correctness.rationale: For a cross-part edge xy with x in V_i and y in V_j, a vertex resolves x,y exactly when it lies in V_i union V_j, so every local-resolving constraint is s_i+s_j>=1 for the part totals s_i. For k=2 there is one constraint and optimum 1. For k>=3, summing all pair constraints gives (k-1) sum_i s_i >= k(k-1)/2, hence objective at least k/2; s_i=1/2 attains it. At equality every pair constraint is tight, and for k>=3 these equations force every s_i=1/2. Thus the optimizer face is exactly as claimed. An independent direct-distance replay verified every local neighborhood through order eight, and the inspected package verifier blob afc61af0042b0b689b4b6fc518ad5d2622b9d050 solves the vertex LP through order ten.
risks: The optimizer classification is by part totals; within each part any nonnegative vertex weights summing to the required total are allowed.
